examples.en: The warmest spot on the floor was cozy, so I fell asleep quickly.
Coming into a warm room, my body thaws.
After drinking the broth, my stomach felt warm.
It's so warm under the blanket that I don't want to get out.

examples.ko: 뜨뜻한 물을 한 잔 마시고 쉬세요.
examples.en: Drink a glass of warm water and rest.
It's warm by the heater but cold by the window.

explain: '따뜻하다'와 같은 계열의 말인데, 느낌이 더 크고 푸근해요. 방바닥, 이불, 국물처럼 몸에 닿거나 몸속으로 들어가는 따뜻함에 잘 어울려요. 활용할 때는 '뜨뜻해요, 뜨뜻한'처럼 규칙으로 변해요.

phrases.example: 추운 날에는 뜨뜻한 방이 제일 좋아요.
phrases.en: On cold days a warm room is the best.
phrases.nuance_ko: 몸이 푸근해지는 따뜻한 방에 잘 어울려요.
phrases.nuance_en: Fits a cozy room that makes your body feel relaxed.

phrases.en: It's warm under the blanket.
phrases.nuance_ko: 지금 느끼는 따뜻함을 해요체로 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The polite form for the warmth you feel now.

phrases.en: I warmed the milk up and drank it.
phrases.nuance_ko: '뜨뜻하게'로 바꾸면 데우는 정도를 말할 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: The '뜨뜻하게' form tells how much you heat something.

explain_en: It belongs to the same family as '따뜻하다' but feels bigger and cozier. It suits warmth that touches your body or goes inside it, such as floors, blankets and soup. It conjugates regularly: 뜨뜻해요, 뜨뜻한.

t90.ax: Drink a glass of warm water and rest.

en: to be smooth; to be sleek

examples.ko: 이끼가 낀 돌이 미끈미끈해서 넘어질 뻔했어요.
examples.en: The mossy stone was slimy, and I almost fell.
When you put this lotion on, your skin feels silky.

examples.ko: 미끈미끈한 해초가 발에 닿아서 깜짝 놀랐어요.
examples.en: I was startled when slimy seaweed touched my foot.
Eel skin is slimy, so it's hard to prepare.

examples.ko: 욕실 바닥이 미끈미끈하면 매트를 깔아 두세요.
examples.en: If the bathroom floor is slippery, lay down a mat.
My hands felt slimy, but they were fine after washing with water.

explain: 기름기나 물기 때문에 매끄럽게 느껴지는 상태를 말해요. 부드러운 피부에는 좋은 느낌으로, 해초나 이끼에는 불쾌한 느낌으로 쓰니 문장 속 대상을 보고 판단해요. '미끈거리다'가 만지는 동안 계속 느껴지는 감촉이라면, '미끈미끈하다'는 그런 상태 자체를 나타내요.

phrases.en: The slimy seaweed was hard to eat.
phrases.nuance_ko: 해초나 이끼처럼 불쾌한 느낌의 대상에 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used for things like seaweed or moss that feel unpleasant.

phrases.en: My skin became smooth after I put on cream.
phrases.nuance_ko: 상태가 바뀌었음을 나타내는 과거형이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The past form showing a change of state.

phrases.en: I like this oil because it doesn't feel slimy.
phrases.nuance_ko: 미끄럽고 번들거리는 느낌이 없어서 만족할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when you're pleased something doesn't feel slick.

explain_en: It describes a smooth feel caused by oil or moisture. It is a good feeling for soft skin and an unpleasant one for seaweed or moss, so the object in the sentence tells you which. '미끈거리다' is the sensation you keep feeling while touching something, whereas '미끈미끈하다' names the state itself.

t90.ax: Eel skin is slimy, so it's hard to prepare.

examples.ko: 전통 혼례에서는 신랑과 신부 뒤에 병풍을 세워요.
examples.en: At a traditional wedding, a folding screen is set up behind the bride and groom.
Mountains and water are painted on the folding screen.

examples.ko: 제사 때 병풍 앞에 상을 차려요.
examples.en: During an ancestral rite, a table is set in front of the folding screen.
There is an old folding screen in my grandfather's room.
A folding screen is stored folded up.
The mountains surround the village like a folding screen.

explain: 혼례, 제사, 돌잔치 같은 전통 행사에서 자주 봐요. 여러 폭을 접었다 펴서 쓰는 가림막이라 '병풍처럼 둘러싸다'는 산이 마을을 감싼 모습을 말할 때 쓰는 비유예요. 친구끼리는 모임에서 가만히 서 있는 사람을 놀리는 말로도 써요.

phrases.example: 친구들 이야기에 끼지 못하고 병풍이 됐어요.
phrases.en: to be left standing around, ignored in a group
phrases.nuance_ko: 모임에서 말도 못 하고 가만히 있는 사람을 놀리듯 말해요. 친구끼리 가볍게 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A casual slang phrase for someone who just stands there without joining in, like a decorative screen.

explain_en: You often see it at traditional events such as weddings, ancestral rites, and first-birthday parties. It is a screen of several panels that folds, so '병풍처럼 둘러싸다' is a figure of speech for mountains wrapped around a village. Among friends it is also a teasing word for someone who just stands still in a group.

examples.en: The farmer sprays pesticide on the field.
The fire truck sprayed water on the fire.
This product works by spraying out a scent.

examples.ko: 차 안에 소독약을 분사하고 문을 닫으세요.
examples.en: Spray disinfectant inside the car and close the door.
The rocket lifted off, ejecting fuel.
If you mist water on the plant, the leaves become moist.

explain: 물, 약, 향기를 좁은 구멍으로 뿜어 뿌릴 때 써요. 집에서는 '뿌리다', '칙칙 뿌리다'를 더 자주 말하고, 설명서나 기계 이야기에서는 '분사하다'를 써요. 뿌리는 도구에는 '스프레이'라는 외래어를 많이 써요.

phrases.en: The machine sprays water like mist.
phrases.nuance_ko: 좁은 구멍으로 물을 뿜을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when water shoots out of a narrow opening.

phrases.en: The scent is sprayed automatically.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뿌려지는 쪽에서 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used from the side of the thing being sprayed.

phrases.en: I spray pesticide with a sprayer.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뿌리는 기계나 도구를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to the machine or tool that sprays.

explain_en: Use it for shooting out water, chemicals or scent through a small opening. At home 뿌리다 or 칙칙 뿌리다 is more common; 분사하다 appears in manuals and talk about machines. For the spray tool itself, the loanword 스프레이 is widely used.

t90.ax: The rocket lifted off, ejecting fuel.

examples.en: Every morning I put the cow back in the barn.
A cow is mooing in the cowshed.

examples.ko: 할아버지 댁 외양간에는 소 두 마리가 있어요.
examples.en: There are two cows in the cowshed at my grandfather's house.

examples.ko: 주말에 가족이 함께 외양간을 깨끗이 청소했어요.
examples.en: On the weekend, my family cleaned the cowshed together.

examples.ko: 외양간 문을 열어 두면 소가 나가요.
examples.en: If you leave the cowshed door open, the cow will go out.
When it started to rain, we brought the cow into the cowshed.

explain: 소나 말을 기르는 집이에요. 요즘 도시에서는 보기 어려워서 속담으로 더 자주 들어요. 발음은 [외양깐]이에요.

phrases.example: 시험이 끝난 뒤에 공부 계획을 짜 봐야 소 잃고 외양간 고치는 거예요.
phrases.en: Making a study plan after the exam is over is just fixing the barn after losing the cow.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일이 잘못된 뒤에야 대비해 봐야 소용없다는 속담이에요. 이미 늦은 행동을 놀리거나 아쉬워할 때 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: A proverb meaning it is useless to prepare only after something has gone wrong. It is used to tease or regret an action that comes too late.
phrases.en_equiv: Closing the barn door after the horse has bolted

explain_en: It is a shed for keeping cattle or horses. Because it is rare to see in cities now, you hear it more often in proverbs. It is pronounced [외양깐].

t90.ax: A cow is mooing in the cowshed.

examples.en: Sunlight came in between the bars of the prison window.
The cat stuck its head out between the bars.
We put bars on the first-floor windows, so it's safe.

examples.ko: 오래된 한옥의 창살 무늬가 정말 예뻐요.
examples.en: The lattice pattern on the old hanok's windows is really pretty.
A bird is sitting on the window bars and singing.

examples.ko: 창살을 잡고 밖을 내다보는 아이가 보였어요.
examples.en: I saw a child holding the bars and looking outside.

explain: 창문이나 문에 일정한 간격으로 대는 가는 막대를 말해요. 쇠로 만든 것은 '쇠창살', 한옥 문의 나무 살도 창살이라고 해요. 감옥 장면에서 많이 나오지만 집 창문에도 흔히 써요.

phrases.en: The window has iron bars on it.
phrases.nuance_ko: 쇠로 만든 창살이고, 튼튼하게 막을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Bars made of iron, used to block something firmly.

phrases.en: I can see the yard through the bars.
phrases.nuance_ko: 창살 바깥쪽을 볼 때 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common pairing for looking beyond the bars.

phrases.en: Hanok doors have wooden lattices.
phrases.nuance_ko: 한옥 문처럼 나무로 짠 창살을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to wooden lattice work like on hanok doors.

explain_en: It means the thin bars set at regular intervals in a window or door. Ones made of iron are called '쇠창살', and the wooden lattice of a hanok door is also '창살'. It comes up a lot in prison scenes, but it is also commonly used for ordinary house windows.

examples.en: The jockey holds a whip and drives the horse.
At the circus, the trainer cracked a whip.
At the sound of the whip, the ox quickened its pace.

examples.ko: 옛날 영화에서 채찍을 쓰는 장면이 나와요.
examples.en: There is a scene in an old movie where someone uses a whip.
Whipping scenes are scary for a child to watch.

examples.ko: 그 말은 저에게 큰 채찍이 되었어요.
examples.en: Those words became a big spur for me.

explain: '당근과 채찍'은 상과 벌을 같이 쓴다는 뜻으로 자주 나와요. '채찍질하다'는 진짜 때리는 것뿐 아니라 '스스로를 채찍질하다'처럼 더 열심히 하도록 몰아붙인다는 뜻으로도 써요.

phrases.example: 좋은 팀장은 당근과 채찍을 함께 써요.
phrases.en: carrot and stick
phrases.nuance_ko: 칭찬이나 상과 벌을 함께 써서 사람을 움직인다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Using praise or rewards together with punishment to motivate people.

phrases.en: push oneself hard
phrases.nuance_ko: 스스로를 더 열심히 하도록 몰아붙인다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Driving yourself to work harder.

explain_en: '당근과 채찍' often appears to mean using rewards and punishment together. '채찍질하다' can mean actually whipping, but also pushing hard to work harder, as in '스스로를 채찍질하다'.

examples.en: My grandmother pulls weeds in the field with a hoe.
While I was digging the soil with a hoe, an earthworm came out.
The hoe rusted, so I bought a new one.
I use a hoe in my balcony garden.

examples.ko: 기념품으로 호미를 사 가는 외국 관광객도 있어요.
examples.en: Some foreign tourists buy a hoe as a souvenir.

examples.ko: 호미 한 자루만 있으면 텃밭 가꾸기가 쉬워요.
examples.en: With just one hoe, tending a garden is easy.

explain: 호미는 손으로 쥐고 땅을 파는 작은 연장이에요. 긴 막대가 달린 큰 '괭이'나 '삽'과는 달라요. 요즘은 한국의 호미가 해외에서도 인기라서 외국 정원사들 사이에서 'homi'라고 불러요.

phrases.example: 작은 문제를 놔뒀더니 호미로 막을 것을 가래로 막게 됐어요.
phrases.en: I left the small problem alone and ended up needing a much bigger effort.
phrases.nuance_ko: 작을 때 해결하지 않아서 나중에 훨씬 큰 힘을 들이게 된다는 속담이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A proverb: failing to fix something when it's small leads to much more effort later.
phrases.en_equiv: a stitch in time saves nine

explain_en: 호미 is a small hand tool for digging and weeding. It differs from the large long-handled '괭이' or '삽' (shovel). Korean hoes have also become popular abroad, where gardeners call them 'homi'.

t90.ax: I use a hoe in my balcony garden.

examples.ko: 그는 본디 조용한 사람이라 말이 별로 없어요.
examples.en: He is quiet by nature, so he doesn't talk much.

examples.ko: 이 건물은 본디 학교로 쓰던 곳이에요.
examples.en: This building was originally used as a school.

examples.ko: 본디 계획은 오늘 떠나는 거였는데 비 때문에 미뤘어요.
examples.en: The original plan was to leave today, but we postponed because of rain.
Do you think people are born good by nature?

examples.ko: 이 노래는 본디 다른 가수가 불렀어요.
examples.en: This song was originally sung by a different singer.

examples.ko: 본디 성격이 급한 편이라 기다리는 게 힘들어요.
examples.en: I am impatient by nature, so waiting is hard for me.

explain: '원래'와 뜻이 같지만 조금 예스럽고 글말 느낌이 나요. 일상 대화에서는 '원래'를 훨씬 많이 말해요.

phrases.en: He is a quiet person by nature.
phrases.nuance_ko: '본디'와 뜻이 같지만 말할 때 훨씬 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning as 본디 but much more common in everyday speech.

phrases.en: This road was originally a narrow country road.
phrases.nuance_ko: '본디'보다 덜 예스럽지만 '원래'보다는 글말에 가까운 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Less old-fashioned than 본디 but more written in tone than 원래.

phrases.example: 고장 난 의자를 원래대로 고쳐 놓았어요.
phrases.en: I fixed the broken chair back to how it was.
phrases.nuance_ko: 처음 상태 그대로 되돌린다고 할 때 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when something is put back exactly as it was at first.

explain_en: It means the same as '원래' but sounds a bit archaic and bookish. In daily conversation people say '원래' much more.

t90.ax: Do you think people are born good by nature?

examples.ko: 담당자가 사고 경위를 소상히 설명해 줬어요.
examples.en: The person in charge explained in detail how the accident happened.

examples.ko: 그 일은 제가 소상하게 알고 있어요.
examples.en: I know that matter in full detail.
The explanation was thorough, so it was easy to understand.

examples.ko: 소상한 안내문 덕분에 어렵지 않게 신청했어요.
examples.en: Thanks to the detailed notice, I applied without difficulty.

examples.ko: 설명서가 소상하지 않아서 몇 번이나 물어봤어요.
examples.en: The manual wasn't detailed enough, so I had to ask several times.

examples.ko: 이 책은 설명이 소상하니까 처음 하는 사람도 따라 할 수 있어요.
examples.en: This book's explanations are thorough, so even a beginner can follow along.

explain: '자세하다'와 뜻이 비슷하지만 빠짐없이 꼼꼼하다는 느낌이고, '소상히 설명하다', '소상히 밝히다', '소상히 알다'처럼 말하거나 아는 내용에 주로 써요. '소상공인'의 '소상'과는 다른 말이에요.

phrases.example: 선생님의 소상한 설명 덕분에 쉽게 이해했어요.
phrases.en: Thanks to the teacher's detailed explanation, I understood it easily.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-ㄴ/은'을 붙여 빠짐없이 꼼꼼한 설명을 꾸며 줄 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The modifier form describes an explanation that is thorough, leaving nothing out.

phrases.en: The company explained the cause of the accident in detail.
phrases.nuance_ko: '소상히'로 바꿔 숨김없이 자세히 알린다는 뜻을 나타내요.
phrases.nuance_en: In the adverb form 소상히, it means making something known in full detail.

phrases.example: 아직 계획이 소상하지 않아서 더 알아봐야 해요.
phrases.en: The plan isn't detailed yet, so I need to find out more.
phrases.nuance_ko: 내용이 충분히 자세하지 않을 때 부정형으로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The negative form is used when the content isn't detailed enough.

explain_en: It is close to '자세하다' but feels thorough, leaving nothing out, and is mostly used with explaining or knowing, as in '소상히 설명하다', '소상히 밝히다' and '소상히 알다'. The '소상' in '소상공인' (small business owner) is a different word.

t90.ax: I know that matter in full detail.

examples.en: In the historical drama, the hero was unjustly branded a traitor.
He was called a traitor who betrayed the king.
It was an era when even a traitor's family was punished.

examples.ko: 역적이 되고 싶은 사람은 아무도 없어요.
examples.en: Nobody wants to become a traitor.
This drama is a story about a traitor.

examples.ko: 친구가 약속을 어겼다고 저를 역적 취급해요.
examples.en: My friend treats me like a traitor because I broke a promise.

explain: 옛날에 나라나 왕을 배신한 사람을 가리켜서 사극에서 많이 들어요. '반역자'보다 사극 느낌이 강하고, 요즘은 약속을 어긴 친구에게 농담으로 '이 역적아' 하고 말하기도 해요.

phrases.en: A loyal subject was branded a traitor overnight.
phrases.nuance_ko: 억울하게 역적이라는 누명을 쓸 때 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A set phrase for being falsely accused of treason.

phrases.en: People called him a traitor.
phrases.nuance_ko: '역적'보다 사극 느낌이 덜하고 더 일반적인 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Less of a historical-drama feel than 역적, and more general.

phrases.en: You broke your promise, you traitor!
phrases.nuance_ko: 친한 친구끼리 농담으로 쓰는 반말 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A joking casual-speech expression between close friends.

explain_en: It refers to someone who betrayed the country or the king in the old days, and you hear it a lot in historical dramas. It feels more like period-drama speech than '반역자', and today people sometimes joke '이 역적아' to a friend who broke a promise.

examples.en: My older brother enlisted as a private second class.
A private second class is the lowest rank in the army.

examples.ko: 아들이 이등병 때 쓴 편지를 아직 가지고 있어요.
examples.en: I still keep the letter my son wrote when he was a private.
The private greeted the senior soldiers.
My uncle rose from private second class to sergeant.
In the movie, a private fires a gun for the first time.

explain: 한국군에서 가장 낮은 병사 계급이에요. 이등병 다음이 '일병', '상병', '병장'이에요. 군 이야기를 나눌 때 '이등병 때', '이등병 시절'이라고 자주 말해요.

phrases.en: My private second class days were the hardest.
phrases.nuance_ko: 군 생활을 돌아볼 때 시기를 말하는 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to refer to a period when looking back on military life.
phrases.en_equiv: when I was a private second class

phrases.en: My younger brother enters the army as a private second class next month.
phrases.nuance_ko: 입대하면 가장 낮은 계급인 이등병부터 시작한다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means one starts at the lowest rank, private second class, upon enlisting.
phrases.en_equiv: to enlist as a private second class

phrases.example: 석 달 뒤에 이등병에서 일병이 돼요.
phrases.en: In three months he is promoted from private second class to private first class.
phrases.nuance_ko: 계급이 올라가는 순서를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to describe moving up in rank.
phrases.en_equiv: to be promoted from private second class to private first class

explain_en: The lowest enlisted rank in the Korean military. After 이등병 come 일병, 상병 and 병장. When people talk about their service, they often say 이등병 때 or 이등병 시절.

en: to be in hiding; to lie low

examples.ko: 형사들이 범인이 올 만한 곳에서 잠복하고 있어요.
examples.en: Detectives are staking out the place where the criminal might come.

examples.ko: 감기 바이러스가 몸속에 잠복해 있다가 피곤하면 나타나요.
examples.en: The virus lies dormant in your body and shows up when you're tired.
The cat lies in wait in the grass and eyes the bird.

examples.ko: 그는 몇 달 동안 조용히 잠복하며 때를 기다렸어요.
examples.en: He lay low quietly for months, waiting for his time.
The reporter waited in hiding at the scene and then took the photo.

examples.ko: 병이 잠복하는 기간은 보통 얼마나 돼요?
examples.en: How long is the incubation period of the disease usually?

explain: 그냥 '숨다'와 달리 때를 기다리며 몰래 숨어 있다는 느낌이 있어요. 수사에서는 '잠복 수사', 병에서는 '잠복기'라는 짝말로 자주 나와요. 일상에서는 '숨어 있다'라고 말해요.

phrases.example: 경찰이 어제부터 잠복 수사를 하고 있어요.
phrases.en: The police have been conducting a stakeout investigation since yesterday.
phrases.nuance_ko: 범인을 잡으려고 숨어서 지켜보는 수사를 말할 때 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A set phrase for an investigation where police hide and watch for a suspect.

phrases.en: This illness has an incubation period of about a week.
phrases.nuance_ko: 병에 걸린 뒤 증상이 나타나기 전까지의 기간을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for the period after infection before symptoms appear.

phrases.en: The criminal was lying in wait near the building.
phrases.nuance_ko: '잠복하다'의 상태를 나타내는 말로, 숨어서 계속 기다리고 있다는 느낌이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes the ongoing state of staying hidden and waiting.

explain_en: Unlike plain '숨다', it implies hiding quietly while waiting for the right moment. It pairs with '잠복 수사' (stakeout) and '잠복기' (incubation period). In daily speech people say '숨어 있다'.

examples.ko: 급하게 돈이 필요해서 시계를 전당포에 맡겼어요.
examples.en: I needed money urgently, so I left my watch at a pawn shop.

examples.ko: 영화에서 전당포 주인이 반지를 살펴보는 장면을 봤어요.
examples.en: I saw a scene in a movie where a pawnbroker examines a ring.
There isn't a single pawn shop in my neighborhood.
I went to retrieve the item I had left at the pawn shop.
My uncle hesitated for a long time in front of the pawn shop.

examples.ko: 전당포를 하시는 할아버지가 금반지 값을 알려 주셨어요.
examples.en: The grandfather who runs a pawn shop told me the price of the gold ring.

explain: '전당포에 맡기다'와 '전당포에서 찾다'를 짝으로 외워 두면 편해요. 영화나 드라마 장면에 나오는 곳이라 이야기 속에서 자주 만나요.

phrases.en: I left my ring at a pawnshop and borrowed money.
phrases.nuance_ko: 물건을 맡기고 돈을 빌릴 때 쓰는 가장 기본적인 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most basic pairing for leaving an item to borrow money.

phrases.en: The pawnshop owner slowly examined the watch.
phrases.nuance_ko: 영화나 이야기에서 자주 나오는 인물이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A character who often appears in films and stories.

phrases.en: I paid back the money and got my watch back from the pawnshop.
phrases.nuance_ko: 맡긴 물건을 돈을 내고 되찾을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when you pay and get back an item you left.
phrases.en_equiv: to get back from a pawnshop

explain_en: It helps to memorize '전당포에 맡기다' (leave at a pawn shop) and '전당포에서 찾다' (retrieve from one) as a pair. It is a place that shows up in movie and drama scenes, so you often meet it in stories.
